primitives.name: assemble
primitives.when: Fit a transcript to a token budget — keep pinned + newest, drop the oldest, rescuing droppable code/doc units as signatures first.
primitives.signature: assemble(units: Unit[], ctx?: AssembleCtx) => Promise<AssembleResult>
primitives.fails: Never throws; with no budget it's identity (nothing dropped). Pinned units exceeding budget are kept best-effort, never a hard cap.
primitives.example:
import { assemble } from 'litectx'
const { units, dropped, tokens } = await assemble(transcript, { budget: 8000 })

primitives.name: compress
primitives.when: Render a code/doc unit at a chosen fidelity (verbatim / signature-only / dropped) to fit a budget.
primitives.signature: compress(node: CompressNode, opts?: { level? }) => Promise<string>
primitives.fails: Never throws; an unparseable node (markdown, preamble, parse failure) falls back to verbatim rather than losing content.
primitives.example:
import { compress } from 'litectx'
const sig = await compress({ text: fnSource, format: 'js', symbol: 'parseConfig' }, { level: 'signature' })

primitives.name: count
primitives.when: Report how much memory a tenant holds ("N facts / M episodes / K docs") without pulling rows.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.count(opts?: { scope?, kind? }) => number
primitives.fails: Throws when `kind` isn't a subset of fact/episode/doc; under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted.

primitives.name: enumerate
primitives.when: Read ALL memory of one kind, gapless + paginated, for "count / all of them" questions recall can't answer (it's ranked + capped). API-only.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.enumerate(opts: { kind: 'fact'|'episode', scope?, offset?, limit?, body? }) => Promise<{ items, total, offset, nextOffset }>
primitives.fails: Throws when `kind` isn't fact/episode, or `offset`/`limit` are not valid non-negative/positive integers; under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted.
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx } from 'litectx'
const ctx = new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() })
let offset = 0, all = []
do { const p = await ctx.enumerate({ kind: 'fact', offset }); all.push(...p.items); offset = p.nextOffset } while (offset !== null)

primitives.name: evict
primitives.when: Drop parked stashes when done — one id, or a bulk age/size policy. API-only; stash-only (never reaches memory).
primitives.signature: liteCtx.evict(sel: string | { olderThan?, maxCount? }) => number
primitives.fails: Does not throw; returns the count removed. Cannot touch a fact/episode by construction — only the stash table.
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx } from 'litectx'
const ctx = new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() })
ctx.evict('stash:toolresult-42')          // one payload
ctx.evict({ maxCount: 100 })              // keep newest 100

primitives.name: forget
primitives.when: Delete written memory — by id, by kind, or tenant-fenced by scope (the correct compliance/erasure primitive: it deletes now). The model calls this directly via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.forget(sel: string | { id?, kind?, by?, scope?, idPrefix? }) => number
primitives.fails: Under `strictScope`, a scope-less memory forget throws (a tenant-blind wipe is unexpressible by omission); combining `{ scope, by }` throws (owner-blind provenance + a fence is the omission footgun). Mem-axis only — never docs/blob/stash.
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx } from 'litectx'
const ctx = new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() })
ctx.forget('pref-theme')                        // one id
ctx.forget({ kind: 'episode' })                 // all episodes
ctx.scoped('tenant:acme').forget({ scope: 'tenant:acme' }) // right-to-erasure for one tenant

primitives.name: get
primitives.when: Fetch the full body behind a recall hit — a whole file/fact, or one chunk (code + its docstring) by line range. The model calls this directly via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.get(id: string, opts?: { startLine?, endLine?, scope? }) => Item | null
primitives.fails: Throws `StalePointerError` when a chunk range is requested from a file that changed since indexing (refuses rather than return different code); returns `null` for an unknown id or a range matching no chunk.

primitives.name: impact
primitives.when: Gauge the blast radius / change-risk of a symbol before editing it. The model calls this directly via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.impact(symbol: string) => Promise<Impact | null>
primitives.fails: Throws `RipgrepMissingError` when `rg` is not on PATH (rather than silently under-counting to a false "isolated"); returns `null` when the symbol isn't in the index.

primitives.name: index
primitives.when: Build or refresh the graph from source before recall/impact — call after files change.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.index(opts?: { paths?, force?, yield? }) => Promise<IndexResult>
primitives.fails: Throws `RipgrepMissingError` only via later `impact()`, not here; a bad `root` throws at construction.

primitives.name: ingest
primitives.when: Store an uploaded document (pdf/docx/md/txt/csv → chunked + searchable; anything else → byte-exact blob) with an optional per-upload scope.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.ingest(buffer: Uint8Array, opts?: { filename?, format?, id?, scope?, expiresAt? }) => Promise<{ id, kind, format, mode, chunks }>
primitives.fails: Throws when a required optional peer dep is missing (pdf → `pdfjs-dist`, docx → `mammoth`) or input exceeds `maxSize`/`maxPages`; under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted.

primitives.name: LiteCtx
primitives.when: You need a litectx store — the entry point for every other primitive.
primitives.signature: new LiteCtx(config: LiteCtxConfig)
primitives.fails: Throws if `config.root` is missing.

primitives.name: liteCtxAsStore
primitives.when: Plug litectx in as a host's memory Store — adapts a LiteCtx to the `{ store, search, get, delete }` shape (e.g. bareagent's socket).
primitives.signature: liteCtxAsStore(lc: LiteCtx, opts?: { kind? }) => { store, search, get, delete }
primitives.fails: Does not throw itself; the returned methods surface litectx's own errors (e.g. `strictScope`).

primitives.name: observe
primitives.when: Record every CE verb call live into a context graph you can export as JSON or Mermaid — drop-in tracing for a run.
primitives.signature: observe(ctx: LiteCtx) => LiteCtx  // proxied; read `.trace`
primitives.fails: Does not throw; `instanceof LiteCtx` still holds on the returned proxy, and tracing is zero-overhead when unused.
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx, observe } from 'litectx'
const ctx = observe(new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() }))
await ctx.recall('auth')
console.log(ctx.trace.mermaid())

primitives.name: peek
primitives.when: Preview a stashed payload's head+tail without paying its full tokens — decide whether to rehydrate. API-only.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.peek(id: string) => { id, bytes, head, tail, createdAt, truncated } | null
primitives.fails: Does not throw; returns `null` for an unknown id.

primitives.name: promotionCandidates
primitives.when: Find episodes recalled often enough to distil into durable facts — the agent-side rung of the promotion ladder. Exposed to the model via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.promotionCandidates(threshold?: number, opts?: { scope? }) => { path, hits }[]
primitives.fails: Under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted; otherwise returns `[]`. litectx flags candidates, never summarizes them (no extraction LLM).

primitives.name: purge
primitives.when: Reclaim storage from expired doc/blob uploads — a scheduled retention sweep (recall already excludes expired rows live).
primitives.signature: liteCtx.purge(opts?: { now?: number }) => number
primitives.fails: Does not throw; returns the count of rows reclaimed (0 when nothing has expired).

primitives.name: recall
primitives.when: Find the most relevant code/docs/memory for a query — ranked search (BM25 + import-spreading, +cosine when embeddings on). The model calls this directly via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.recall(query: string, opts?: { kind?, n?, body?, scope? }) => Promise<Hit[] | Record<kind, Hit[]>>
primitives.fails: Never throws on a miss — returns `[]` (or per-kind `{}`); a single stale chunk under `body:true` is nulled, not thrown; throws only under `strictScope` when a doc-kind query omits `scope`.

primitives.name: recentActivity
primitives.when: Answer "what was I working on" — the code/doc chunks litectx witnessed edited most recently.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.recentActivity(opts?: { days?, since?, limit? }) => { id, symbol, kind, lastEditedAt, edits }[]
primitives.fails: Does not throw; empty until real edits are observed (a cold/`force` first build logs none — loading isn't editing).

primitives.name: recentMemory
primitives.when: Ground on the latest written memory when a query has no rankable term (all-stopword "what did I say") and `recall` returns `[]`. Exposed to the model via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.recentMemory(opts?: { kind?, scope?, n?, body? }) => (Hit & { createdAt, occurredAt? })[]
primitives.fails: Under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted; throws if one call mixes the doc axis with fact/episode (distinct scope stores). Logs no recall (recency is not demand).

primitives.name: remember
primitives.when: Persist a fact/episode/doc so it survives across sessions and is recallable by meaning. The model calls this directly via MCP.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.remember(id: string, text: string, opts?: { kind?, by?, occurredAt?, scope? }) => Promise<void>
primitives.fails: Throws when `kind` is not one of fact/episode/doc; under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted. Re-`remember`ing the same `(scope, id)` supersedes in place (no duplicate row).
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx } from 'litectx'
const ctx = new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() })
await ctx.remember('pref-theme', 'user prefers dark mode', { kind: 'fact', by: 'human' })
await ctx.remember('ep-1', 'deploy failed on missing env var', { kind: 'episode' })

primitives.name: reviewCandidates
primitives.when: Surface agent-asserted facts that proved useful (recalled ≥ threshold) for a human to validate or discard.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.reviewCandidates(threshold?: number, opts?: { scope? }) => { path, hits }[]
primitives.fails: Under `strictScope`, throws when `scope` is omitted; otherwise returns `[]` when nothing crossed the threshold.

primitives.name: scoped
primitives.when: Serve many tenants from one instance — bind a scope once and every verb on the view is fenced to it.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.scoped(scope: string | symbol) => ScopedView
primitives.fails: Throws at creation on a bad bind (null / omitted / non-string non-GLOBAL) — a scope-less scoped view is impossible.
primitives.example:
import { LiteCtx, GLOBAL } from 'litectx'
const ctx = new LiteCtx({ root: process.cwd() })
const acme = ctx.scoped('tenant:acme')      // every verb fenced to acme
await acme.remember('pref-1', 'prefers dark mode', { kind: 'fact' })
const shared = ctx.scoped(GLOBAL)            // shared knowledge-base tier

primitives.name: stash
primitives.when: Drop a large payload (tool result, page dump) from the context window, keeping only a cheap handle to rehydrate later. API-only — adopter code chooses this, never a model verb.
primitives.signature: liteCtx.stash(id: string, text: string) => void
primitives.fails: Does not throw; upserts by `id` (a re-stash replaces). A stash is never indexed or recalled — reachable only by exact `id` via `get`/`peek`/`evict`.

primitives.name: summaryWindow
primitives.when: Keep the last-N turns verbatim under budget pressure and fold older ones into one rolling summary (the host supplies the summarizer).
primitives.signature: summaryWindow(units: Unit[], ctx?: SummaryWindowCtx) => Promise<{ units, dropped, tokens }>
primitives.fails: Never throws; falls back to a plain `assemble` when unwired, when everything fits, or when there are < 2 older turns to fold — never worse than FIT.
primitives.example:
import { summaryWindow } from 'litectx'
const out = await summaryWindow(transcript, { budget: 8000, keepRecent: 6, summarize: async (t) => callModel(t) })

primitives.name: toWriteAction
primitives.when: Build the gate-able action for a memory write, to hand to a wired guardrails `writeGate.check` before persisting.
primitives.signature: toWriteAction(id: string, text: string, opts?: { kind?, provenance?, meta?, injectionRisk? }) => WriteAction
primitives.fails: Pure — never throws, no I/O, no judgment; it only shapes the action (the gate decides the outcome).

primitives.name: trim
primitives.when: Evict old turns from a running transcript (by size or count) and get back the dropped units with content, so you can harvest-before-evict.
primitives.signature: trim(units: Unit[], policy?: TrimPolicy) => Promise<TrimResult>
primitives.fails: Throws `TypeError` when `units` is not an array; with no policy set it's a no-op (keep all). Never splits an atomic group or drops a pinned unit.
